elena: Quick check — how should the gateway attribute quota/cost for requests that we transcode REST -> gRPC vs native gRPC calls? This impacts the per-route billing view in Console and the canary signals.

nate: Do you mean billing attribution (which customer/route) or telemetry deduping (so we don't double-count latency)? :thinking:

elena: Both, sorry. Example: mobile client calls /v1/generate (REST) -> gateway transcodes to modelsvc.Generate (gRPC). Console currently shows both the edge route and the backend RPC. That inflates token counts in the route dashboard.

srini: We ran into this with the caching rollout. Two options: 1) attribute to original incoming route (simpler for product owners) or 2) split attribution: edge request + backend compute. Each has pros/cons for quotas and SLOs.

marta: If we pick #1, we need a clear column in Console for "compute-only tokens" so infra can see cost separated from fronting traffic. Otherwise infra teams end up penalized for product traffic.

nate: Implementation idea: add a request header when gateway forwards, e.g. `X-Redwood-Origin-Route: /v1/generate` + `X-Redwood-Forwarding-Units: 120` then the backend increments a compute counter but we only show the compute counter as a sub-metric. UI can surface either stacked or collapsed.

srini: Be careful — headers can be spoofed if we ever accept direct client traffic to the backend. Need mTLS or signed attestations. Also telemetry pipelines need a route id mapping so we can join edge and backend spans without duplicating.

marta: Agree on signed attestation. For joins, we can use a PG-managed mapping table of route_id -> backend_id and include a short trace id in the header for sampling.

elena: How would this affect quota enforcement? If we attribute to incoming route, quotas will be consumed there. But Dedicated customers expect per-backend capacity commitments.

nate: For Dedicated we should enforce at both layers: edge checks customer route quota (to throttle abuses) and backend enforces compute pool caps (for isolation). The Console quota panel should show both: "Route quota used" and "Pool quota used" and when a request is blocked we show which layer.

srini: Telemetry-wise we need a dedup key so analytics don't sum tokens twice across dashboards. Proposed key: `trace_id + attribution_mode`. If attribution_mode = "edge" we count only once; if = "split" we emit two metrics with roles `edge`/`compute`.

marta: UI UX ask: during rollouts we run mixed mode (some customers routed to new grpc backend, others stay on REST). Can we have a per-rollout toggle that switches Console to show "unified" view (merged) vs "split" view (edge vs compute)? Product managers want easy toggles.

elena: That's the ask. Also need to ensure billing exports (CSV/BigQuery) use the same logic as Console so customers see consistent charges.

nate: Ops concern: A/B routing can produce spikes where both edge and backend metrics show increased latency if counts are doubled. We should add a "rollout mode" flag emitted as a metric label so alerts know to ignore expected inflation during rollout windows.

srini: Implementation sketch (envoy filter snippet):
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: >
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local origin = request_handle:headers():get(":path")
        request_handle:headers():add("x-redwood-origin-route", origin)
      end
```
This sets the origin header; downstream service can read and attach compute units to metrics.

marta: Nice. We should gate this behind a feature flag and a rollout percent so we can test telemetry joins.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for header-attribution v1 -> 10% of edge traffic :rocket:

elena: OK next steps from here:
- srini: prototype telemetry join + dedup key (logs -> metrics)
- nate: implement header + secure signing for Dedicated paths
- marta: add UI toggle mockups for unified vs split view
- elena: coordinate billing export mapping and communicate to finance

Any objections?

nate: No objections. I'll make a spike PR for the header + signature.

srini: I'll drop a small dataflow job to test deduping with sampled traces.

marta: I'll put mockups in Figma and post link tomorrow.

elena: Thanks all. If you hit edge cases ping me. :eyes:
